title: Non-bearer auth schemes: custom API-key header and HTTP Basic
description: The two bounded extensions spec 9.2 permits after Bearer, deferred out of the first valid consumption flow (reading recorded on WCLI-9). Spec 9.2: Support Bearer authentication first. Add a custom API-key header and HTTP Basic only if they pass the same safety tests; these are bounded extensions, not reasons to delay the first valid consumption flow. Bearer ships with WCLI-9 and WCLI-10. Neither scheme may land without the same approval-binding (T13-class) and credential non-disclosure (T14-class) evidence bearer carries; the audit half additionally needs WCLI-11.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A custom API-key header scheme passes the same safety tests as bearer: a changed header name, auth alias or binding cannot reuse an approval (T13-class), and the credential reaches only the approved header and is absent from argv, environment, files, output and audit (T14-class)
HTTP Basic passes the same safety tests, with the username source and exact byte shape recorded in the approved snapshot and never interpolated into a URL or a non-auth header
An unsupported or unknown auth type is rejected at approval time without echoing the submitted type or value, and a change of auth type invalidates any prior approval
